summary: This work develops a theoretical framework for optimizing Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana (LZSM) single-qubit gates in fluxonium circuits, incorporating multilevel dynamics, leakage mitigation, and open-system dissipation. Fast, high-fidelity Y(π/2) rotations are demonstrated with gate errors approaching $10^{-5}$ at 2 ns and $10^{-5}$ at 1.3 ns in optimal architectures accounting for environmental decoherence.
motivation: LZSM protocols offer speed advantages over resonant Rabi-driven gates in low-frequency qubits with large anharmonicity, but standard two-level analytical tools neglect multilevel structure and strong-drive-dependent dissipation that become critical in real fluxonium devices.
method: The authors derive analytical solutions via the counter-rotating hybridized rotating-wave approximation (CHRW) and a Floquet-Schrieffer-Wolf (FSW) effective Hamiltonian accounting for qubit-frequency renormalization by higher levels, identify leakage-suppression valleys at privileged frequencies $\omega_d = \omega_{21}/n$ ($n \geq 2$), and analyze open-system fidelity using a Floquet-Born-Markov master equation capturing drive-amplitude-dependent $T_1(A_e, \omega_d)$ from dielectric loss.
result: For a moderate architecture with $\{E_J, E_C, E_L\} = \{4, 1, 1\} \times 2\pi$ GHz ($\omega_{10}/2\pi = 0.58$ GHz, $\alpha/2\pi = 2.81$ GHz), LZSM gates achieve infidelity $\sim 10^{-5}$ and $t_g \approx 1.92$ ns; optimization across architecture space reveals regimes around $E_L/E_J \sim 0.1$ and $E_C/E_J \sim 0.5$ achieving $\mathcal{F}_g > 0.99995$ with $t_g < 1.3$ ns at $T_b = 15$ mK and $T_1^0 = 500$ μs.
